text:
[IMG]

Consider the above reaction, the major product "P" formed is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Concentrated HBr protonates the –OH group, and loss of water gives a secondary carbocation on the carbon bearing the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group; this carbon is allylic to the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ group.

The allylic cation is a resonance hybrid: the positive charge is shared between that secondary carbon and the terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ carbon, so $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ can bond at either end.

Bonding at the secondary carbon gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2})-\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (option A), which has only a 1,1-disubstituted C=C. Bonding at the terminal carbon (allylic shift) gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br})-\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, whose C=C is trisubstituted and still conjugated with the ester C=O.

In concentrated HBr the allylic bromides re-ionise and equilibrate, so the more stable, more substituted alkene, methyl 2-(bromomethyl)but-2-enoate, is the major product.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $[Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3-}$, $[Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3-}$ and $[Co(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3-}$ are $d^{2}sp^{3}$ hybridised.

Statement II : $[MnCl_{6}]^{3-}$ and $[FeF_{6}]^{3-}$ are paramagnetic and have 4 and 5 unpaired electrons, respectively.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is false
Both statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, Mn is +3 with $3d^{4}$. Strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the electrons as $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{0}$ (one paired and two single electrons in three 3d orbitals), so two 3d orbitals stay empty and the hybridisation is $d^{2}sp^{3}$, with 2 unpaired electrons.

In $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, Fe is +3 with $3d^{5}$. Strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ gives $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, leaving two 3d orbitals empty: $d^{2}sp^{3}$, with 1 unpaired electron.


[IMG]

In $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$, Co is +3 with $3d^{6}$. With $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, oxalate causes pairing, giving $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$: $d^{2}sp^{3}$ and diamagnetic. Statement I is correct.


[IMG]

In $[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ causes no pairing, so $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{4}$) is high spin, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$, with 4 unpaired electrons ($sp^{3}d^{2}$).


[IMG]

In $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ causes no pairing, so $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{5}$) is high spin, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$, with 5 unpaired electrons ($sp^{3}d^{2}$). Both are paramagnetic with 4 and 5 unpaired electrons, so Statement II is correct.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
To an aqueous solution containing ions such as $Al^{3+}, Zn^{2+}, Ca^{2+}, Fe^{3+}, Ni^{2+}, Ba^{2+}$ and $Cu^{2+}$ was added conc. HCl, followed by $H_{2}S$.

The total number of cations precipitated during this reaction is/are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In conc. HCl the high $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]$ suppresses the ionisation of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ (common-ion effect), so $[\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}]$ is very low and only sulphides of extremely low $K_{sp}$ (group II) are precipitated.

$\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ forms black $\mathrm{CuS}$ ($K_{sp}\approx 10^{-36}$), which precipitates even from strongly acidic solution.

$\mathrm{Zn}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ need the much higher $[\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}]$ of ammoniacal medium (group IV) to precipitate as $\mathrm{ZnS}$ and $\mathrm{NiS}$.

$\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is only reduced by $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ to $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ (with separation of sulphur), and $\mathrm{FeS}$ does not form in acid; $\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+}$ is precipitated only as $\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{3}$ in group III; $\mathrm{Ca}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Ba}{}^{2+}$ give no sulphide precipitate.

So only one cation, $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$, is precipitated.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
The equilibrium constant for the reaction

A(s) $⇌$ M(s) + $\frac{1}{2}O_{2}(g)$

is $K_{p} = 4$. At equilibrium, the partial pressure of $O_{2}$ is $_________$ atm. (Round off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the given equilibrium, the solid substances do not contribute to the equilibrium constant expression since their activities are considered to be 1.

For the reaction:

$\text{A(s)}⇌\text{M(s)}+\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2}(\text{g})$

The equilibrium constant, $K_{p}$, is given by:

$K_{p}=P_{\text{O}_{2}}^{n}$

where $P_{\text{O}_{2}}$ is the partial pressure of $\text{O}_{2}$ and $n$ represents the stoichiometric coefficient of $\text{O}_{2}$ in the balanced chemical reaction, which is $\frac{1}{2}$. Therefore, the expression for $K_{p}$ becomes:

$K_{p}=\left (P_{\text{O}_{2}}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$

Given that $K_{p}=4$, substituting into the equation gives:

$4=\left (P_{\text{O}_{2}}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$

To find $P_{\text{O}_{2}}$, square both sides of the equation:

$4^{2}=P_{\text{O}_{2}}$

$16=P_{\text{O}_{2}}$

Thus, the partial pressure of $\text{O}_{2}$ at equilibrium is $16$ atm.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

When 400 mL of $0.2 M H_{2}SO_{4}$ solution is mixed with 600 mL of 0.1 M NaOH solution, the increase in temperature of the final solution is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{-2} K. ($Round off to the nearest integer).

[Use : $H^{+} (aq) + OH^{-} (aq)$ $\to$ $H_{2}O$ : $\Delta_{γ}$H = $-$57.1 kJ mol$^{-1}$]

Specific heat of $H_{2}O = 4.18 J K^{-1} g^{-1}$

density of $H_{2}O = 1.0 g cm^{-3}$

Assume no change in volume of solution on mixing.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$n_{H^{+}}=\frac{400\times 0.2}{1000}\times 2=0.16$

$n_{OH^{-}}=\frac{600\times 0.1}{1000}=0.06$ (L.R.)

Now, heat liberated from reaction = heat gained by solutions

or, 0.06 $\times$ 57.1 $\times$ $10^{3}$

= (1000 $\times$ 1.0) $\times$ 4.18 $\times$ $\Delta$T

$\therefore$ $\Delta$T = 0.8196K

= 81.96 $\times$ $10^{-2} K$ $\approx$ 82 $\times$ $10^{-2} K$

text:
3 moles of metal complex with formula $Co(en)_{2}Cl_{3}$ gives 3 moles of silver chloride on treatment with excess of silver nitrate. The secondary valency of Co in the complex is $___________$.

(Round off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Three moles of complex give three moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$, so each formula unit has one ionisable chloride and the complex is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}$:

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{AgNO}{}_{3}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}+\mathrm{AgCl}$

The secondary valency equals the coordination number: each bidentate en supplies two donor atoms and each coordinated chloride one, so $2\times 2+2=6$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
In a solvent 50% of an acid HA dimerizes and the rest dissociates. The van't Hoff factor of the acid is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{-2}$.

(Round off to the nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the initial amount of HA be $a$ mol; $0.5a$ mol dimerises and the remaining $0.5a$ mol dissociates.

Dimerisation, $2~\mathrm{HA}(\mathrm{HA}){}_{2}$, turns $0.5a$ mol of HA into $0.25a$ mol of dimer.

Dissociation, $\mathrm{HA}\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+\mathrm{A}{}^{-}$, turns the other $0.5a$ mol of HA into $0.5a$ mol of $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ and $0.5a$ mol of $\mathrm{A}{}^{-}$.

Total particles $=0.25a+0.5a+0.5a=1.25a$.

$i=\dfrac{1.25a}{a}=1.25=125\times 10^{-2}$

Hence, the answer is 125.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift
